From: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acme-data.com>

Subject: Cutover today — quick sprint and smoke coordination

Hi team,

We are starting the VPC cutover at 10:00 PT today for the Acme Data private deployment. Want to run a short activation sprint and then hand off to Acme ops for 2-hour post-go-live monitoring. Can you confirm the following before 09:30 PT?

- Runbook version you will be executing (we have runbook_activation_v2.pdf attached to this thread).
- Smoke test matrix and expected pass thresholds (latency P95, error %).
- KV cache priming plan and IP ranges we need to whitelist for warmup traffic.
- Telemetry endpoints (Grafana / tracing) we should monitor and a link to the transient trace we should watch for prefix-warmup.
- Rollback triggers and who to page if we need to abort.

We plan to provide a firewall egress file and BGP peer IPs before cutover. Window is 10:00–10:30 PT for traffic shift and 10:30–12:30 PT for immediate smoke validation.

Contacts during the window: Taylor (cell: +1-415-555-0199) and Jessica (netops).

Thanks,
Taylor
NetOps, Acme Data

Attachment: pre-cutover-checklist (sent internally)

- Smoke matrix: Marissa will paste the matrix below and attach the CSV.
- KV warmup: we'll send warmup traffic from our testing fleet to the listed prefix ranges. Please ensure NATting allows 52.23.10.0/24 and 34.201.45.0/25.

I will be on the bridge at 09:45 PT to confirm last-minute network ACLs. Attaching runbook_activation_v2.pdf to this thread for your reference.

—

Planned smoke matrix (summary) — full CSV attached (smoke_matrix.csv):

1) Connectivity checks (0–10m)
   - TCP 443 to inference endpoints from 3 test clients (expected: 100% success)
   - BGP adjacency state (expected: Established within 30s)

2) Latency/Throughput (10–40m)
   - P50/P95 token-generation latency against baseline model: pass if P95 < 400ms and no >10% regression vs baseline
   - Throughput validation: steady-state QPS within +/-15% of pre-cutover

3) Functional correctness (10–60m)
   - 20 prompt set checks for response length/format and truncated tokens; 0 failures allowed in first 30m

4) KV cache + warmup (first 20m)
   - Expect KV cache hit rate >65% by 20m; capture kv_warmup_log.txt for audit

5) Observability sanity (throughout)
   - Traces show prefix warmup events; error spike regression alerts suppressed for 30m to avoid noise.

Quick ops play: if any of the top 3 checks fail, we pause traffic shift and execute rollback step 2. Karthik, I'll need confirmation you can run a quick ACL patch if we see NAT issues.

—Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: smoke_matrix.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Brooks <taylor.brooks@acme-data.com>, Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acme-data.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T12:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cutover today — quick sprint and smoke coordination

Post-go-live quick readout (summary of 10:00–12:30 PT window):

- Traffic shift: completed at 10:17 PT. No packet-loss at the fabric layer observed. BGP adjacency flapped for ~18s during propagation but recovered; no action needed.
- Connectivity: TCP 443 success 100% from test clients (3 regions).
- Latency: P95 token gen peaked at 520ms at 10:23 but returned to ~380ms within 7 minutes. Baseline regression of ~8% — within our threshold.
- Functional checks: 20 prompts run; 1 minor formatting deviation in prompt #14 (investigating root cause; likely model variant mismatch).
- KV warmup: hit rate reached 68% at 19m. Attached kv_warmup_log.txt for timestamps and sample keys used.
- Telemetry: dashboards and traces in related_links show expected prefix-warmup pattern. No sustained error-alerts triggered.

Issues and mitigations: observed transient SYN drop on a subset of clients between 10:20–10:26 PT (suspected MTU path misconfiguration). Mitigation: we adjusted path MTU on the NAT gateway and retried; subsequent connections succeeded. No rollback required.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: follow-up on functional deviation and add 10 extra prompts to regression set (due 2026-10-01).
- Mina: send final handback note to Acme with timeline and link to artifact folder (today EOD).
- Karthik: open a tracking ticket for MTU detection in E2E checks (JIRA SUP-4521).

Summary: cutover succeeded, minimal transient noise recovered automatically. Handing over to Acme for extended monitoring; Redwood will keep oncall for 48h.

—Karthik
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
